links.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade, Reading Ease) of GPT-4 initial responses versus recommended sixth-grade level
links.effect: GPT-4 initial responses had FK grade 13.06 and Flesch Reading Ease 36.87, similar to Google (12.24; 40.05), well above the recommended sixth-grade level.
links.quote: GPT-4’s initial responses had a Flesch-Kincaid grade level of 13.06, a Flesch Reading Ease score of 36.87, and a word count of 222.80.

links.outcome: Readability of GPT-4 output after prompting to rewrite for low literacy versus initial output
links.effect: After the low-literacy rewrite prompt, FK grade fell from 13.06 to 6.58 and Reading Ease rose from 36.87 to 76.20 (P<0.001), with similar word count (218.6 vs 222.8).
links.quote: However, when GPT-4 was prompted to make its responses more readable, the Flesch-Kincaid grade level improved to 6.58, the Flesch Reading Ease score to 76.20, and the word count slightly decreased to 218.60.

links.outcome: Agreement of GPT-4 numerical answers with Google answers for CDA FAQs
links.effect: 60% (6 of 10) of numerical responses differed between GPT-4 and Google, e.g., success rate 62.40% (Google) vs above 80% (GPT-4).
links.quote: In our study, 60% of numerical responses differed between GPT-4 and Google, underscoring the variability and potential inaccuracy in AI-generated health content.

models_evaluated: GPT-4 (ChatGPT Plus with Browse with Bing)

links.effect: Initial GPT-4 vs Google: Flesch-Kincaid 13.06 vs. 12.24 (P=0.41); Reading Ease 36.87 vs. 40.05 (P=0.53).
links.quote: No significant differences were found in readability between GPT-4 and Google, displaying a similar Flesch-Kincaid grade level (13.06 vs. 12.24, P=0.41) and Flesch Reading Ease score (36.87 vs. 40.05, P=0.53).

links.effect: Prompted rewrite lowered Flesch-Kincaid to 6.58 from 13.06 and raised Reading Ease to 76.20 from 36.87; P<0.001.
links.quote: Upon prompting GPT-4 to improve the readability of its responses, GPT-4 showed a lower Flesch-Kincaid grade level (6.58 vs. 13.06 vs. 12.24, P<0.001) and a higher Flesch Reading Ease score (76.20 vs. 36.87 vs. 40.05, P<0.001).

links.effect: 60% of numerical responses differed between GPT-4 and Google.
links.quote: In our study, 60% of numerical responses differed between GPT-4 and Google, underscoring the variability and potential inaccuracy in AI-generated health content.
